newsitem.title: USA: Georgian diplomat involved in fatal car crash.
newsitem.headline: Georgian diplomat involved in fatal car crash.

text.p: A Georgian diplomat was involved in a five-car collision on Friday night that killed a teenage girl and police were investigating whether or not to file charges against him, a Washington police spokesman said on Saturday.

The spokesman said a 1987 Ford Taurus driven by Gueorgui Makharadze, 35, a Georgian diplomat, struck a car and went spinning into three other cars including one being driven by Joviane Waltrick, 16, of Kensington, Maryland.
Waltrick was pronounced dead shortly after the accident. Makharadze was taken to Georgetown Hospital but was released on Saturday with what an embassy spokesman called minor injuries.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement that Georgian authorities have been asked for their cooperation in the investigation.

"We have notified the ambassador of the Republic of Georgia that we consider this a very serious matter," Burns said. "It is State Department policy to request a waiver of diplomatic immunity if local prosecutors pursue criminal charges."
Georgian embassy spokesman Misha Siamashvili, speaking to reporters, expressed condolences to the family of the victim on behalf of his government and his country.
The district attorney's office has been asked to investigate the case to determine if charges should be filed against Makharadze, a police spokesman said.
Last Thursday New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani asked for the recall of two diplomats from Russia and Belarus involved in a punchup with New York police.

The incident erupted after police officers pulled the Russian from his car because he appeared intoxicated and refused to show his driver's license after being ticketed for illegal parking near a fire hydrant. They said the Belarus diplomat then jumped out and punched one of the policemen.
